botany.native_range: The eastern Mediterranean, from Greece and the Balkans through Anatolia and the Levant to the western Himalayas.
botany.habitat: Rocky slopes and dry hill country on well-drained, often poor soil. Also widely planted as an ornamental and as a windbreak.
botany.climate: Mediterranean: hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters.
distinguishing_characteristics: A very narrow, dense, columnar crown, in the familiar 'pencil' form.
Dark green, scale-like foliage held close to the branches.
A trunk that stays slender even on old trees.
interesting_facts: The columnar form is prized so much that it has been selected for for millennia; wild trees are broader and irregular.
Cypress wood is aromatic and resistant to decay, and has long been used in Mediterranean construction.
botany.attribution: Botanical summary compiled for Arboretum. Verify against the Kew Plants of the World Online record for Cupressus sempervirens before treating any specific figure as authoritative.
